text:
anya: FYI i'm hitting a weird stall in our kotlin sample app when cancelling a Retrofit suspend call that streams a large response. after cancel, the next request blocks until socket timeout even though coroutine job is cancelled. repro is highest on Pixel 8 with corporate VPN, but i saw one case on Pixel 6 too.
vik: interesting. is the body.close() being invoked? streaming with readTimeout=0 can leave sockets open if you never consume/close body.
anya: our suspend endpoint returns ResponseBody and we rely on Retrofit's suspend adapter to close when coroutine finishes. we cancel the coroutine before reading whole body.
rob: that pattern can leak the underlying socket if the response is mid-read. OkHttp historically required explicit body.close() or response.close().
anya: we tried wrapping with use { } and explicit close in finally but the stall still happens intermittently.
mika: did you upgrade OkHttp recently? some 4.x -> 5.x changes altered HTTP/2 stream shutdown semantics.
anya: we just upgraded to OkHttp 5.0.0-beta last week to pick up perf fixes.
vik: that could be it. 5.x changed how streams are marked as canceled vs closed over HTTP/2; some platforms with aggressive NAT (VPN) leave streams in half-closed state until full TCP FIN.
anya: sample snippet:
```kotlin
suspend fun fetch() : String = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
  val resp = api.streamLarge()
  // we cancel before reading all bytes in some flows
  resp.string()
}
```
rob: try attaching an EventListener and enable OkHttp logging. also add coroutine.invokeOnCancellation { call.cancel() } in the suspend wrapper so the call is cancelled at the HTTP layer when coroutine is cancelled.
mika: also consider setting connectionPool().evictAll() as short-term mitigation and testing with keepAlive disabled to confirm.
anya: disabling keepAlive removed it in my quick test but unacceptable perf hit. evictAll reduced frequency but not gone. adding call.cancel() in invokeOnCancellation seems promising locally.

dev-bot: linked issue created: #6221 "OkHttp 5 cancel vs stream close race on Android devices behind VPN"
vik: another angle: check interceptor ordering. If a network interceptor delays closing the response (e.g., for metrics), cancel path might not propagate immediately.
anya: good point 11 we have a metric interceptor that reads headers and schedules a coroutine to record body size async. could be holding things. i'll audit it.
anya: i'll open a draft PR that adds a Kotlin suspend helper which registers invokeOnCancellation to call.cancel(), adds an option in the SDK builder to enable auto-cancel-on-coroutine-cancel, and documents the OkHttp 5+ Android edge. will also add a small instrumented repro test on Pixel 7/8 with VPN emulator.
rob: that sounds like a solid mitigation. please include EventListener logs in the issue.
mika: tag infra to run matrix with OkHttp 4.x vs 5.x and with/without VPN to confirm regression.
anya: PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1452 (work in progress)
vik: once PR passes CI, let's ship opt-in and consider enabling by default in next major if no perf regression.
dev-bot: CI: presubmit checks started for pr/1452
anya: thanks all. adding notes to onboarding docs about streaming cancellation caveat and sampleapp snippet. will follow up in issue. :raised_hands:
